sources.role: Pinned kernel-checked foundation for the integrated baseline
Direct exact-pin dependency and upstream home for reusable algebraic-geometry infrastructure
sources.compatibility: The root Mazur package and its separate upstream-contract workspace both depend on Tau Ceti a3913fd with Lean 4.33.0-rc1 and mathlib 79d0395. CI rejects pin drift between them.

sources.license: Mixed branch status: curated files carry Apache-2.0 headers, but this branch has no root LICENSE
sources.role: Audited prior art and selective porting source for Picard, cohomology, finite-group-scheme, isogeny, and open Y_0(N) infrastructure
sources.compatibility: The Lean compiler matches, while AINTLIB's mathlib pin is 266 commits newer. Three explicitly Apache-2.0, placeholder-free modules are now selectively ported at the Mazur pin: the monoidal sheaf foundation, Scheme.Pic, and CartierDual. The larger relative-Picard and MuN cones remain excluded by the option and license gates.

roadmap_impact.headline_treatment: The selected foundations are integrated without changing theorem-completion weights; the remaining estimate stays folded into the conservative 12% ecosystem-readiness figure.

progress.method: A node earns no theorem-progress credit for a statement alone. A proof node earns 70% for an isolated kernel proof, 85% after API review, and 100% only after a downstream consumer compiles. Infrastructure earns 40% when its definitions compile, 70% after mathematical sanity checks, and 100% after a real downstream consumer compiles. The headline is the weighted sum.

nodes.title: The five-coset bound on X_1(11)
nodes.summary: Carry out the explicit five-isogeny descent showing that the five visible torsion points represent every coset modulo 5E(Q).

challenge.informal: Every rational point on y^2 + y = x^3 - x^2 differs from one of the five multiples of (0,0) by five times a rational point.
challenge.recommended_route: Complete the Kummer/Selmer calculation around the explicit five-isogeny and Miller function already recorded in XOneElevenDescent.

nodes.title: Exclude exact rational order 11
nodes.summary: Feed the five-coset bound through the existing X_1(11) reduction and classification.

artifacts.name: MazurTorsion.XOneEleven.rationalPoint_addOrderOf_ne_eleven
artifacts.description: Consume the five-coset contract and the existing X_1(11) reduction to exclude exact rational order 11.

nodes.title: Classify the noncuspidal rational points on X_1(13)
nodes.summary: Show that the explicit genus-two order-13 model has no rational affine point with x different from 0 and -1.

challenge.signature:
theorem xOneThirteen_no_noncuspidal_point
    (x y : ℚ) (hx0 : x ≠ 0) (hxnegOne : x ≠ -1)
    (hcurve : y ^ 2 =
      MazurTorsion.Kubert.orderThirteenHyperellipticPolynomial x) :
    False := sorry
challenge.informal: The explicit X_1(13) sextic has no rational affine point away from the cusp abscissas 0 and -1.
challenge.recommended_route: Use the prepared Pell certificate and a genus-two Jacobian or descent argument, or supply another kernel-checked rational-point classification.

nodes.title: Classify the noncuspidal rational points on the order-18 curve
nodes.summary: Show that the explicit genus-two order-18 model has no rational point with x different from 0 and 1.

challenge.signature:
theorem xOneEighteen_no_noncuspidal_point
    (x y : ℚ) (hx0 : x ≠ 0) (hx1 : x ≠ 1)
    (hcurve : y ^ 2 =
      MazurTorsion.Kubert.orderEighteenHyperellipticPolynomial x) :
    False := sorry
challenge.informal: If y^2 equals the explicit order-18 sextic at a rational x, then x is 0 or 1.
challenge.recommended_route: Finish the classical Eisenstein π=3+ω descent using the primitive descent data already proved, or give another kernel-checked rational-point classification.

nodes.title: Exclude exact rational order 25
nodes.summary: Prove that no rational point on an elliptic curve over Q has exact additive order 25.

challenge.signature:
theorem no_rational_point_of_order_twentyFive
    (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic]
    (P : (E⁄ℚ).Point) :
    addOrderOf P ≠ 25 := sorry
challenge.informal: An elliptic curve over Q has no rational point of exact order 25.
challenge.recommended_route: Develop a Tate-normal-form or modular-curve reduction with an independently checkable descent endpoint.

nodes.title: Exclude exact rational order 35
nodes.summary: Prove that no rational point on an elliptic curve over Q has exact additive order 35.

challenge.signature:
theorem no_rational_point_of_order_thirtyFive
    (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic]
    (P : (E⁄ℚ).Point) :
    addOrderOf P ≠ 35 := sorry
challenge.informal: An elliptic curve over Q has no rational point of exact order 35.
challenge.recommended_route: Reduce to explicit compatible 5- and 7-isogeny data and close the resulting modular or Diophantine endpoint.

nodes.title: Bridge exact order 49 to the X_0(49) correspondence
nodes.summary: Turn an exact rational order-49 point into a noncuspidal point of the already classified level-seven correspondence.

challenge.signature:
theorem no_rational_point_of_order_fortyNine
    (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic]
    (P : (E⁄ℚ).Point) :
    addOrderOf P ≠ 49 := sorry
challenge.informal: An elliptic curve over Q has no rational point of exact order 49.
challenge.recommended_route: Use the compiled orderSevenG7F, exists_orderSevenHauptmodul_of_exactOrder, orderSevenQuotient, and orderSevenPointMap APIs; prove that the explicit Vélu point function respects addition or multiplication by seven; then carry an exact order-49 point through the nonbacktracking branch and apply XZeroFortyNine.no_noncuspidal_correspondence_point.

nodes.title: Assemble all finite-level exclusions
nodes.summary: Remove all four composite callbacks and the separate 11 and 13 prime callbacks from PointOrder.

artifacts.name: MazurTorsion.rationalTorsion_orders_mem_cyclicOrders_of_finite_endpoints
artifacts.description: Combine the exact order 11, 13, 18, 25, 35, and 49 exclusions into the finite-endpoint point-order API.

nodes.title: Finite support of orders of rational functions
nodes.summary: Prove that a nonzero rational function on a Noetherian integral scheme has nonzero order at only finitely many codimension-one points, then instantiate Tau Ceti's OrderSystem.

challenge.signature:
theorem finite_support_orderAt
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsNoetherian X]
    (g : Additive X.functionFieldˣ) :
    (Function.support fun x : TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.CodimensionOnePoint X =>
      TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeWeilDivisor.orderAt x g).Finite := sorry
challenge.informal: A nonzero rational function on a Noetherian integral scheme has nonzero order at only finitely many codimension-one points.
challenge.recommended_route: Prove the global finiteness theorem upstream in Tau Ceti, then use it to package the existing local order maps as an OrderSystem.

nodes.title: Degree-zero product formula on a proper smooth curve
nodes.summary: Prove that every principal divisor on a proper smooth geometrically integral curve has residue-degree-weighted degree zero.

artifacts.name: TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeWeilDivisor.orderSystem_isWeightedDegreeZero
artifacts.description: State and prove the residue-degree-weighted product formula for every nonzero rational function on a proper smooth curve.

challenge.signature:
theorem divisorProductFormula
    (K : Type u) [Field K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsNoetherian X]
    (π : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsProper π] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 π]
    (S : TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilDivisor.OrderSystem
      (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.CodimensionOnePoint X)
      (Additive X.functionFieldˣ))
    (hord : S.ord = TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeWeilDivisor.orderAt) :
    S.IsWeightedDegreeZero (fun x ↦ (π.residueDegree x : ℤ)) := sorry
challenge.informal: For the geometric order system of a smooth proper integral curve, every principal divisor has residue-degree-weighted degree zero.
challenge.recommended_route: Prove the residue-degree-weighted product formula for Mathlib's orders of vanishing, then use the checked weighted PicZero transport into the scheme Picard group.

nodes.title: Dimension of a product of abelian varieties
nodes.summary: Prove that Tau Ceti's abelian-variety dimension is additive under its product construction.

challenge.signature:
theorem prod_dim {K : Type u} [Field K]
    (A B : AbelianVariety K) :
    (AbelianVariety.prod A B).dim = A.dim + B.dim := sorry
challenge.informal: The dimension of A × B is dim A + dim B for abelian varieties over a field.
challenge.recommended_route: Reduce Tau Ceti's topological Krull dimension of the product scheme to the corresponding scheme-theoretic product-dimension theorem.

challenge.signature:
theorem divisorLineBundleDictionary
    (K : Type u) [Field K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsNoetherian X]
    (π : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsProper π] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 π]
    (S : TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilDivisor.OrderSystem
      (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.CodimensionOnePoint X)
      (Additive X.functionFieldˣ))
    (hord : S.ord = TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeWeilDivisor.orderAt) :
    Nonempty (MazurTorsion.AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorPicard.Dictionary S X) := sorry
challenge.informal: For the geometric order system of a smooth proper integral curve, prove the full invertible-sheaf/Picard comparison and identify divisor classes with the scheme Picard group. Checked code proves these two outputs are equivalent to the complete dictionary. Affinely, it constructs the actual tensor-additive tilde line bundles, a canonical Picard embedding with exact principal kernel, an unconditional range equivalence, and a full equivalence under exactly the reverse tensor-unit/local-rank-one comparison.
challenge.recommended_route: Import the companion chart and descent modules. Prove `AffineChart.DedekindOrderCompatibility` for Dedekind affine charts and construct `PicardIso.PullbackMonoidalData` (or port the exact pinned upstream pullback-monoidal cone without source-level options). The checked API then transports the exact chart kernel, class descent, and range equivalence to `Pic(U)`. For a canonical affine coordinate cover, construct a divisor-indexed additive system of `CurveDivisorDescent.DivisorCocycle` values by proving localization compatibility for the specified Picard-representative affine line bundles. Prove object-specific `LineBundleDescent.EffectiveInvertible` for those cocycles; cover-wide invertible effectivity, or module effectivity plus locality of invertibility, are stronger sufficient inputs. Global principal triviality additionally needs coherent triviality for the chosen principal cocycles and `ModuleDescentEssentiallyInjectiveFor`, which follows from fully faithful module descent. Separately discharge tilde reflection for the forward Picard comparison; canonical Picard surjectivity is equivalent to the reverse comparison. The weighted product formula remains the independently registered A2 Challenge.
